THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:

The petitioner has been charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 376(A), 354(A),
506, 420 of the Indian Penal Code ('the IPC' for short).
2. The summary of the charge sheet is that the petitioner and the survivor got acquainted with each other when respondent No.2 was working with the father of the petitioner.
The acquaintance ended up in love relationship.

On 16.04.2021, the petitioner called upon the survivor to NC:
2023:KHC:41472 come to Bangalore and thereafter, the petitioner took the survivor to a lodge where he mixed drugs in the water and thereafter committed forcible sexual intercourse without her consent from 16.04.2021 and 17.04.2021.

The petitioner is alleged to have video graphed the survivor on his mobile phone then he committed forceful sexual intercourse and stated that, he will not marry her and if she reveals it to anyone, he threatened that he would upload her video on porn sites and social media sites.
Thereafter, the petitioner by promising to marry her has committed the offences alleged.

3. Sri Vivek Subba Reddy, the learned Senior counsel for the petitioner submit that the alleged incident had taken place from 16.04.2021 to 17.04.2021, and the First Information Report ('the FIR',
for short) was lodged before the Tirupathi East Police Station, Tirupathi on 08.05.2022 without offering plausible explanation.

He further submits that in the absence of any allegation that the petitioner induced the survivor to have sexual intercourse by NC: 2023:KHC:41472 promising to marry with an intention to cheat, the continuation of the criminal proceedings would be an abuse Sri Ajay Raghav M vs State Of Karnataka on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42185932/
2 process of law.

v. M. Madhusudhan Rao reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582.
4.

On the other hand counsel for respondent No.2 submits that the charge sheet material clearly discloses that the petitioner and survivor visited the lodge at Bangalore on the said dates and the veracity of the allegations against the petitioner can be considered at the time of the trial and it cannot be gone into this petition.

He further submits that the delay in lodging the FIR cannot be considered for quashing the impugned proceedings when charge sheet material prima-facie discloses that the commission of the offences alleged by the petitioner.

Learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State would reiterate the submissions made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
6. Considered the submission made by the learned counsel for the parties.
The allegation in the charge sheet is that the petitioner and survivor got acquainted with each other in the year 2015 and the said acquaintance turned into love relationship.
It is alleged that the petitioner by promising to marry induced respondent No.2 to come to Bangalore and thereafter drugging her, committed forcible sexual intercourse without her consent.
The alleged incident had taken place from 16.04.2021 to 17.04.2021.
Initially, the complaint was filed by respondent No.2 before the before the Disha police station on 31.03.2022.
Since, the FIR was not registered, the petitioner lodged the FIR in the East Police Station on 08.05.2022.
The FIR initially was lodged nearly after 10 months from the date of the alleged incident without NC: 2023:KHC:41472 offering any plausible explanation.
The parties were allegedly in relationship for more than 6 years.

7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582 has held as follows:
"30.

entities.text: State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Time and again, the object and importance of prompt lodging of the first information report has been highlighted.
Delay in lodging the first information report, more often than not, results in embellishment and exaggeration, which is a creature of an afterthought.

A delayed report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, the danger of the introduction of a coloured version, an exaggerated account of the incident or a concocted story as a result of deliberations and consultations, also creeps in, casting a serious doubt on its veracity.

Therefore, it is essential that the delay in lodging the report should be satisfactorily explained."
8.

In the instant case, there is no allegation that the petitioner with an intention to cheat, induced the survivor to have sexual intercourse by promising to marry which is the essential element to constitute the commission of the offences of cheating and rape.

Therefore, the very basic elements of allegations are consequently absent and having regard to the fact that the petitioner and the NC:
2023:KHC:41472 survivor were in relationship for more than 6 years
, it is inferred that the FIR was lodged only after the relationship between the parties was strained.

Therefore, the continuation of Sri Ajay Raghav M vs State Of Karnataka on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42185932/
3 investigation against the petitioner will be an abuse of the process of law.

ORDER i.
The criminal petition is allowed.
ii. The impugned proceedings in S.C.No.597/2023 on the file of LIII Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru(CCH-54) is hereby quashed.
